title: Prepay Pool Smoothing and SLA Crediting — pooled prepaid capacity with rolling credits and autoscale safety net
creator: Priya Menon
description: Problem: Enterprise buyers want the predictability of reserved GPUs but also flexibility for burst and seasonality. Current committed-reserve products are rigid (monthly/annual commits) and lead to wasted capacity or complex contract addenda. Proposal: introduce a pooled prepay product (tenant-level or portfolio-level) that smooths prepaid GPU credits over a rolling window, converts predictable unused commit into time-boxed burst credits, and pairs with a metered autoscale safety net that automatically taps on-demand capacity while crediting usage to the pool. This ticket scopes pricing/packaging rules, SLA tier definitions by throughput band, contractual language for credit conversion and failover, and the security questionnaire/contract updates required for enterprise procurement. Key goals: 1) reduce first-year sticker shock for large commits, 2) preserve forecastable revenue, 3) minimize operational exposure from unexpected burst demand, 4) keep security/compliance approvals aligned with Private/Dedicated procurement. This is a product + legal + finance + security cross-functional initiative.
acceptance_criteria: PRD reviewed and approved by PM, Finance, Legal and Security
Top-level pricing sheet with at least 3 prepaid pool SKUs (monthly, quarterly, annual) and clear conversion rules for unused credits
SLA tier definitions aligned to throughput bands with measurable SLOs (p99 latency, guaranteed throughput lanes)
Autoscale safety net behavior defined: trigger thresholds, billing reconciliation, and automated crediting flow for pooled users
Draft contract addendum and updated enterprise SQ template produced and passed initial legal review
Pilot plan: at least one customer committed for a 3-month pilot with instrumentation plan and KPI dashboard defined
notes: Trade-offs considered: (a) aggressive smoothing reduces short-term revenue recognition predictability for Finance vs. higher conversion rate from trials to commits; (b) making burst credits auto-convert risks gaming without throttles; propose caps and decays on converted credits
Metric targets: reduce unused-commit churn by 25% in first 6 months; pilot target gross margin >= current reserved SKU margin minus 5%

Pricing models to evaluate: fixed price per GPU-hour with smoothing multiplier; tiered per-throughput band with blended on-demand uplift; hybrid where unused commit converts to X hours of 'burst credit' with 30-day expiry

Operational concerns: need support from infra (quota engineering) for per-tenant pooled buckets, telemetry updates for credit accounting, and billing reconciliation flows between prepaid pool and on-demand usage

Security/QS items: update enterprise security questionnaire to reflect that pooled prepay can be used with Dedicated or Private; include expected data handling, KMS usage, and audit log retention fields for contract negotiation
Legal ask: create contract language for non-fungible credits, expiration, refund windows, and breach-of-SLA remediation (crediting tiers and penalty caps)
